item.text: I’ll read the selected lyric and reconstruct the Urdu body from its Roman transcription.

---
title: "مارے گئے شبیرؑ فضا میں یہ صدا ہے"
language: "Urdu"
lang: "ur"
direction: "ltr"
kalamType: "Noha"
tags: ["noUrdu"]
aliases: []
published: false
---

Maray gaye Shabbir fiza may ye sada hay
Zainab tera pardes may koyi na raha hay

1
Maa kehti thi may aa ke mana loon tumhe Asghar
Ik baar pukaro mera dil doob raha hay

2
Afsos ke ye qatil e Akbar ne na jana
Naiza to Muhammad ke kalejay pe laga hay

3
Hamsheer se milnay ko bohat tarrpa hay Akbar
Atki hui sanson may bhi Sughra ki sada hay

4
Fizza ne soey nehr ye Ghazi ko sada di
Abbas utho khatray may Zainab ki rida hay

5
Kal pehray pe Abbas thay aur aaj hay Zainab
Aey sham e gharibaan ye ajab tarz e jafa hay

6
Kon aa ke Sakina ko tamachon se bachaye
Bhai Ali Akbar hay na Abbas chacha hay

7
Islam bachanay ko Asar dasht e sitam may
Ashoor ke din khoon bahattar ka baha hay

python - <<'PY'
from pathlib import Path
import subprocess
p = Path('src/data/lyrics/mare-gaye-shabbir-fza-mein-ye-sada-hai.md')
old = subprocess.check_output(['git', 'show', f'HEAD:{p}'], text=True).split('---', 2)[2].strip()
_, metadata, body = p.read_text().split('---', 2)
roman = '\\n'.join(line.removeprefix('  ') for line in metadata.split('romanLyrics: |-\\n')[1].splitlines()).strip()
assert roman == old
blocks = body.strip().split('\\n\\n')
assert len(blocks) == 8
assert len(blocks[0].splitlines()) == 2
for number, block in zip('۱۲۳۴۵۶۷', blocks[1:]):
    assert len(block.splitlines()) == 3 and block.splitlines()[0] == number
print('Original Roman transcription preserved. Urdu opening and seven two-verse stanzas verified.')
PY"

item.text:
Reconstructed the Urdu body in the selected lyric and preserved the Roman transcription in `romanLyrics`. Verified that both versions contain the two-verse opening and seven numbered two-verse stanzas. Updated the text direction to right-to-left and removed `noUrdu`.

I read “soey nehr” as `سوئے نہر` and the closing takhallus “Asar” as `اثر`.
